lesson.title: BAGS: Adjectives Before the Noun
lesson.subtitle: Beauty, Age, Goodness, Size (beau, jeune, bon, petit, grand, nouveau) — the high-frequency rebels that step in front.

hook.title: Why Short Everyday Adjectives Step in Front: BAGS
hook.content: Colors and specific descriptions follow the noun (un café noir). Only one small club of short, everyday adjectives steps IN FRONT of the noun — remembered by BAGS: Beauty (beau, joli), Age (jeune, vieux, nouveau), Goodness (bon, mauvais), and Size (grand, petit)!

footnotes.title: Why beau, nouveau, and vieux wear an -l coat before masculine vowels
footnotes.content: Before a masculine noun starting with a vowel or mute H (ami, homme, hôtel), beau, nouveau, and vieux use bel, nouvel, vieil so the final /l/ links smoothly: un bel hôtel, un nouvel ami, un vieil homme!

pattern.title: BAGS in Front, Colors in Back
pattern.content: Put BAGS between the article and the noun (une belle ville, un bon restaurant), and flank the noun when combining BAGS + color (une petite maison blanche).
pattern.linguist_note: Pre-nominal placement is restricted to a closed class of short evaluative adjectives.
pattern.trap_note: Never write *un beau hôtel — before a masculine vowel or mute H, use bel, nouvel, vieil (un bel hôtel)!

exercises.prompt: Match each BAGS adjective with its feminine form and prevocalic masculine form:
exercises.target_answer: Beauty: beautiful / handsome, Age: new, Age: old, Beauty: pretty, Age: young
exercises.meaning: beau → belle (bel before m. vowel), nouveau → nouvelle (nouvel before m. vowel), vieux → vieille (vieil before m. vowel), joli → jolie, jeune → jeune (invariable)
exercises.explanation: bel/belle, nouvel/nouvelle, and vieil/vieille sound identical in the mouth!

exercises.prompt: What is the word-for-word French order of 'Une petite maison blanche'?
exercises.meaning: Literal structure: A small house white
exercises.explanation: Size (petite, BAGS) steps in front of maison, while color (blanche) stays behind it!

exercises.prompt: How do you say 'a beautiful hotel' (l'hôtel is masculine and starts with a mute H)?
exercises.explanation: Before a masculine vowel/mute-H noun, beau becomes bel: un bel hôtel!

exercises.idea: it is a beautiful city and a good restaurant
cues: It is a beautiful city → C'est une belle ville
and a good restaurant → et un bon restaurant
idea_parts: first noun phrase → C'est une belle ville
second noun phrase → et un bon restaurant
exercises.target_answer: C'est une belle ville et un bon restaurant
exercises.meaning: It is a beautiful city and a good restaurant
exercises.explanation: Both belle and bon belong to BAGS and precede their nouns.

diagnosis.slip: placed belle or bon after the noun
diagnosis.cue: BAGS adjectives precede the noun: une belle ville, un bon restaurant.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.spoken: C'est un nouveau restaurant dans une jolie ville
exercises.target_answer: C'est un nouveau restaurant dans une jolie ville
exercises.meaning: It's a new restaurant in a pretty town
exercises.explanation: Both nouveau (Age) and jolie (Beauty) step in front of their nouns.
exercises.affirmation: You placed both nouveau and jolie before their nouns.

summary.outcome: Place BAGS adjectives before the noun and use bel/nouvel/vieil before masculine vowels.

use_example.german: Un petit café noir dans un bel hôtel.
use_example.english: A small black coffee in a beautiful hotel.

summary.takeaway: BAGS steps in front, colors stay in back — and beau/nouveau/vieux wear -l before a masculine vowel.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on Le Pont ([12] The Near Future): see how BAGS: Adjectives Before the Noun leads directly into The Near Future.

twist.prompt: Think it through again without looking back — express "It is a beautiful city and a good restaurant" in French:
twist.target_answer: C'est une belle ville et un bon restaurant
twist.explanation: Re-constructing "C'est une belle ville et un bon restaurant" from the underlying rule cements the pattern of BAGS: Adjectives Before the Noun.

beau.etymology_derivation: BAGS adjective: steps before the noun! Becomes bel before a vowel (un bel hôtel) and belle in the feminine.

jeune.etymology_derivation: Already ends in -e, so masculine and feminine are identical.

vieux.etymology_derivation: Becomes vieil before a vowel (un vieil ami) and vieille in the feminine.

bon.etymology_derivation: Latin bonus 'good' — English borrowed the word back as 'bonus', a good thing added.

petit.etymology_derivation: English 'petite' is the French feminine form, borrowed whole — the masculine is petit.

grand.etymology_derivation: English 'grand' came straight from French; the feminine adds a silent -e, which wakes the silent d into sound: grand /ɡʁɑ̃/ → grande /ɡʁɑ̃d/.

nouveau.etymology_derivation: Steps before the noun; nouvel before a vowel, nouvelle in the feminine.

ville.etymology_derivation: Latin vīlla 'country estate' grew into the whole city in French (leaving 'city' as la cité for the historic core).

hôtel.shift_rule: Norman doublet: S and H dropped
hôtel.etymology_derivation: Latin hospitalis → hostel AND hôtel — the same word entered English twice: once with its S (hostel, hospital), once without (hôtel).

restaurant.etymology_derivation: From restaurer 'to restore' — originally a restoring broth sold in Paris in 1765.
